title: Reliable and Efficient Amortized Model-based Evaluation
one_line: AIMS: embedding->Rasch difficulty + Fisher CAT; amortization tested only on within-dataset question split.

title: Item Response Scaling Laws: A Measurement Theory Approach for Efficient and Generalizable Neural Scaling Estimation
one_line: AIMS: IRT abilities transfer across benchmarks sharing a measurement objective, after one-time calibration.

title: AI Measurement Science (textbook)
one_line: Official: amortized IRT for cold start; CAT requires pre-calibrated item parameters.

title: LLM Evaluation on Unseen Questions: Contextual Multidimensional IRT Model
one_line: Embedding-conditioned MIRT: cross-scenario item ranking for a fixed LLM falls to AUC~0.5; model ranking transfers better.

title: 100 instances is all you need: predicting the success of a new LLM on unseen data by testing on a few instances
one_line: Generic instance-level assessors degrade out of distribution; 'inherent predictability of LLMs is low'.

title: PredictaBoard: Benchmarking LLM Score Predictability
authors: Pacchiardi, Voudouris, Slater, Martinez-Plumed, Hernandez-Orallo, Zhou, Schellaert
one_line: Benchmark of instance-level score predictors with explicit in- vs out-of-distribution splits.

title: Anticipatory Evaluation of Language Models
one_line: LLMs forecast benchmark accuracy from task descriptions (post-cutoff) with MAE ~9.9 pts at high confidence; offline-only for us.

title: Lost in Benchmarks? Rethinking Large Language Model Benchmarking with Item Response Theory
one_line: Item difficulties rarely exceed 1.0 while frontier abilities exceed 3.0: easy benchmarks are a realistic draw.

title: Observational Scaling Laws and the Predictability of Language Model Performance
one_line: LM capabilities lie in a low-dimensional space predictable from public scores: the subject side is the transferable signal.

title: tinyBenchmarks: evaluating LLMs with fewer examples
authors: Maia Polo, Weber, Choshen, Sun, Xu, Yurochkin
one_line: IRT anchors + gp-IRT estimator; needs prior responses on target benchmark; use gp-IRT as external baseline.

title: metabench -- A Sparse Benchmark of Reasoning and Knowledge in Large Language Models
one_line: IRT-selected <3% subset reconstructs scores; a single common factor dominates.

title: Anchor Points: Benchmarking Models with Much Fewer Examples
one_line: Anchor selection requires model outputs on the dataset; not applicable to cold benchmarks.

title: Fluid Language Model Benchmarking
authors: Hofmann, Heineman, Magnusson, Lo, Dodge, Sap, Koh, Wang, Hajishirzi, Smith
one_line: Ablation: at 10 items most validity gain comes from IRT aggregation; adaptive selection mainly cuts variance; needs calibrated items.

title: Cost-Efficient Estimation of General Abilities Across Benchmarks
one_line: MIRT + V-optimal selection: <7% MAE on unseen tasks after 16 items, but target-task items are calibrated.

title: You Don't Need to Run Every Eval
one_line: 84x133 model-benchmark matrix is ~rank-2; a second ability factor is not worth building given our 4% interaction variance.

title: Active Testing: Sample-Efficient Model Evaluation
one_line: Acquisition proportional to surrogate expected loss; uniform when the predictor is item-agnostic.

title: Active Statistical Inference
one_line: Label where the model is uncertain; equal uncertainty implies uniform sampling, predicting our random ~ smart null.

title: Capitalization on item calibration error in adaptive testing
one_line: Info-based selection on noisy item parameters harms estimation; argues against re-opening acquisition on a rho~0.3 Jev prior.

title: A Global Information Approach to Computerized Adaptive Testing
one_line: KL 'global' information preferred early in a test (metadata-verified); use an expected-Brier/KL rule if acquisition is re-opened.

title: In-season prediction of batting averages: A field test of empirical Bayes and Bayes methodologies
one_line: EB/hierarchical shrinkage beats the raw small-n binomial rate in every scenario.

title: A weakly informative default prior distribution for logistic and other regression models
one_line: Cauchy/t default prior wins CV across many datasets; Cauchy did not replicate on our 4-5 benchmark groups.

title: Position: Don't Use the CLT in LLM Evals With Fewer Than a Few Hundred Datapoints
one_line: CLT intervals badly undercover at small n; Bayesian/Beta-binomial recommended.

title: A New Vector Partition of the Probability Score
one_line: Brier = uncertainty - resolution + reliability (metadata-verified); decompose B0 loss per fold (E1).

title: LLMs Show No Signs Of Individuated Metacognition
one_line: LLM confidence reduces to one shared item-difficulty factor: Jev carries beta (shared), not subject-specific, information.

title: Time Travel in LLMs: Tracing Data Contamination in Large Language Models
one_line: Instance-level contamination detectable via guided instruction; test whether Jev rho is inflated on pre-cutoff benchmarks (E2a).

title: Estimating problem difficulty without ground truth using Large Language Model comparisons
one_line: Pairwise LLM difficulty + Bradley-Terry (r>=0.80 vs humans); candidate upgrade of Jev scoring (E2b).

title: Question Difficulty Estimation for Large Language Models via Answer Plausibility Scoring
one_line: Entropy of answer plausibility as LLM difficulty; open-QA only, not LOBO-tested.

title: Measuring all the noises of LLM Evals
one_line: Prediction noise E[p(1-p)] is large and predictable; consistent with our 20-27% within-cell share and a Brier floor ~0.07.

title: Adding Error Bars to Evals: A Statistical Approach to Language Model Evaluations
one_line: Questions as a super-population sample with clustered SEs; supports the hierarchical benchmark->pair bootstrap.
